### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2ee7f2c41017aa1b5e018434cb0dba64d6a1c0ae` — the merge of head `a43bf0a98999f25655ccd18cf4db62842456aead` into base `59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2ee7f2c41017aa1b5e018434cb0dba64d6a1c0ae && git checkout 2ee7f2c41017aa1b5e018434cb0dba64d6a1c0ae
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59 a43bf0a98999f25655ccd18cf4db62842456aead && git checkout -B drift-repro 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59 && git merge --no-ff a43bf0a98999f25655ccd18cf4db62842456aead

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 59547058aeb3eccde6f267293367dabf5ef82e59` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a43bf0a98999f25655ccd18cf4db62842456aead`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-empty-search-fields-refusal.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-search-empty-set.test.ts, .changeset/27732-engine-empty-search-fields.md + packages/spec/src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.ts, packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts (`QuerySchema.searchFields`, `FullTextSearchSchema.fields`), packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts (the three `Engine*OptionsSchema.searchFields`, lines 190/514/559), packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts (`resolveSearchFields`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts (`assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`findData` 13282-13299, `narrowStoredMetadataSearch` 5194), packages/runtime/src/stored-metadata-reader-seam.ts (`refuseOrNarrowStoredMetadataEvaluate`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts:540-560, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts:1290-1300,1507, content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx (the prose face, read to judge the sentence, not reviewed), docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md (the disposition vocabulary)

Read on this head: card #27732 (body and its 4 comments: 6519259214, 6519918549 triage, 6520880971 claim, 6523412292 os-dev-report), PR #28108 (body, 5-file list, net diff `origin/main...a43bf0a9`, 1 PR comment: the docs-drift advisory), the check-runs on `a43bf0a9` at 2026-10-30T13:11Z, and the live tree (`origin/main` 9cbe5079 and the head). Not read: the dispatch order, the seat's own conclusions.

Check-runs at my reading: complete and `success` — Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, TypeScript Type Check, Type Check · source gates / debt ledger / consumer gates / workspace, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected, Plan Test Core shards, Test Core (2/8), Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Auto Label, filter. Still `in_progress`: Test Core shards 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Path-skipped: the UI lanes, the dogfood shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, the opt-in harnesses. No failure among the complete ones; the seven open shards are the queue guard's to wait on, and this record says nothing about their outcome.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each read in the code, not the PR body:

1. **`ObjectQL.find` / `findOne` / `count` / `aggregate` refuse `searchFields: []`** — right. `refuseSearchOverrideNamingNoField` (engine.ts 751-768) runs at the top of `expandSearchOnAst` (13434-13438), which is the one expander all four verbs reach (`find` 13717→expand, `findOne` 14047→expand, `count`/`aggregate` through `expandSearchOnOptions`, whose early return fires only when both keys are `undefined`). An array is taken as sent, so `[]` → `names.length === 0` → throw before `resolveSearchFields` and before any driver call. Status 400, code `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `param: 'searchFields'`: the envelope `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable` throws at the door for the same value (protocol-query-validation.ts 889-897), so `mapDataError` serves both callers alike; the new test pins the parity against `findData` on the same engine.
2. **The object-form `search: { query, fields: [] }` is refused on its own slot** (`param: 'search.fields'`) — right, and it is the card's item 1 exactly: `FullTextSearchSchema.fields` is `searchFieldsArray()` (`.min(1)`), which the three `Engine*OptionsSchema.search` members reuse, so the engine-side declaration already refused this value while the engine tolerated it. Judged whenever `raw` is an object, independently of a sibling `searchFields`; that is stricter than the door's `searchFields ?? search.fields` precedence (protocol.ts 13282-13289) but identical to the declaration, which refuses `fields: []` regardless of the sibling, and a `POST` body carrying both is refused by the body schema before the door gate. The engine never admits a value either declaration refuses: right.
3. **A comma string naming no field (`' , '`, `''`) is refused** — right. The string arm is the door's own derivation (split, trim, drop blanks) and the accept set `search-fields-names-a-field.ts` publishes (`[^\s,]`). The `GET` transport spelling reaches the engine as sent through `findData`, so refusing it in process is the same rule, not a second one. A non-blank string keeps the pre-existing `resolveSearchFields` tolerance: not this card.
4. **Absent and `null` still search the default set** — right. `typeof null !== 'string'`, `Array.isArray(null)` is false → `names === undefined` → return; the control test pins it. `ENGINE_FIND_OPTION_KEYS` is untouched, so no option key is added or removed.
5. **Refused whether or not a search term rides along, and for a system context** — right, and it is the door's own posture (protocol.ts 13278-13281: "checked whether or not a `search` term rode along"). A `count({ searchFields: [] })` with no `search` reaches the expander because the early return needs both keys `undefined`.
6. **Non-string array members, objects, numbers** — left to the expansion's existing handling. The door refuses these `INVALID_FIELD`; the declarations refuse them at parse. Not narrowed here, and the docblock says so. Right to leave, and correctly named as not this card.
7. **The flipped pin in `engine-search-empty-set.test.ts`** — right. `[]` no longer reaches the empty-set refusal (`INVALID_FIELD`, `param: 'search'`) because it is refused first; the three named overrides keep the #24284 pin intact. This is the narrowing's own consequence, not a fix-to-green.
8. **Public surface** — no export, type or option key changes; `FullTextSearchSchema` is newly imported into engine.ts from `@objectstack/spec/data`, which engine.ts already imports from. The message's closing words are read off `FullTextSearchSchema.shape.fields.safeParse([])` (`SEARCH_FIELDS_NAMES_NO_FIELD`) rather than copied: one source. (`lazySchema` proxies `.shape`; the spec's own test at search-fields-names-a-field.test.ts:135 reads it the same way.) Right.
9. **In-repo producer census, read in the tree** — no non-test producer hands the engine an empty override: `protocol-record-reads.ts:551-558` passes `searchFields` only when the queryable subset is strictly narrower and skips an object left with none; `data-action-routes.ts:1296-1300,1507` keeps the empty list so `findData` refuses it, which it already does since #27484; the stored-metadata narrowing returns a non-empty list or throws. The UI (REST client) sends `searchFields` only when `searchableFields` is non-empty. Right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/27732-engine-empty-search-fields.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`, title `fix(objectql)!:`, a **BREAKING** banner, both declaration lines, and one ADR-0087 marker. Matches the diff: one released package moves (`@objectstack/objectql`), the change narrows a runtime accept set, and `Metadata-protocol: none` is right — no authorable key, value or type changes (the one authorable `searchFields` in the spec is the retired `element:record_picker.searchFields` tombstone, untouched; a view's `searchableFields` is not read here). AGENTS.md § Post-Task Checklist 3: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition — so `patch` with `!` is the prescribed level, not an understatement. `Check Changeset` and the ADR-0087 gate (in `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`) are `success` on this head.

`Clause-②:` line — `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — …` at line start in both the PR body and the changeset, the one spelling `readClause2Line` reads; the arm is the first token inside the parenthesis. Correct: the diff widens nothing and narrows the engine's runtime accept set; triage 6519918549 directed exactly this spelling. ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right — the body carries no FROM/TO table or rewrite block; "The remedy" is a one-line fix of a call, not a metadata migration, and the marker's reason names what the gate re-verifies (no key added, removed, renamed or re-shaped; no export change).

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []` — none to answer.

Dev deviations, each answered:
- *Commit trailers, model-free pair* — the repo's rule; not reviewed here.
- *Refusal as a module-private function in engine.ts rather than a sibling module (the #27008 shape)* — accepted. The #27008 shape that matters is the mechanism (refuse at the one expander, before any read, in the declaration's words, the door's envelope), and that is met; the claim's file surface named `engine.ts`. No finding.
- *Dogfood battery on `bdbb4799`, not `a43bf0a9`* — verified in the tree: `git diff bdbb4799 a43bf0a9` touches one file, the new unit test, +10/−5, all type assertions (`as any` → `as unknown as Engine*Options`) and a docblock. Runtime-identical; the head's own `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run is `success`. Accepted.
- *No assignees / review requests* — the os-dev rule; no finding.

Dev `out_of_scope_findings`, each answered:
- *(1) the runtime reader-context seam* — real, read in the tree (see ④, S1). Dev says "Carrier: seat", nothing filed: escalated as should-fix S1.
- *(2) #28059, the engine-side declarations* — confirmed: filed, triaged p2 `domain:spec` (6522171038), claimed by `domain:spec#1` (6523197991) with `data-engine.zod.ts` as its surface. Right carrier. One sentence it does not name: see S2.
- *(3) #28082, the dogfood pin PR #27964 rewrote* — pre-existing main red on `origin/main`, not this diff; the head's dogfood gate is green. No finding.
- *(4) the all-unknown override tolerance of `resolveSearchFields`* — pre-existing, correctly left; "noted, not filed" loses it: should-fix S3.

Item 2 of the card (the comma-string asymmetry) — triage 6519918549 ruled it by design and not changed; the PR records it and widens nothing. Premise holds. No flag outstanding at the lane boundary; nothing escalated beyond the three should-fixes.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`: `QuerySchema.searchFields` and `FullTextSearchSchema.fields` (query.zod.ts 455, 557) declare `searchFieldsArray()` = `z.array(z.string()).min(1, SEARCH_FIELDS_NAMES_NO_FIELD)` since PR #27725; `QueryTransportParamsSchema.$searchFields` declares the string and array arms of the same set; the door has refused the set since #27484. So the capability "pass an empty override and have it read as absent" is declared nowhere: the canonical declaration refuses it, the doors refuse it, and the only place it survived was the in-process engine's `resolveSearchFields` tolerance. This PR makes the spec's own refusal real at the engine; it takes nothing away that a declaration promised. The one declaration that still admits `[]` is the engine's own option type, `Engine{Query,Aggregate,Count}OptionsSchema.searchFields` (data-engine.zod.ts 190/514/559, pinned admitted by search-fields-names-a-field.test.ts:149), so for the window until #28059 lands the engine refuses what its own bag type admits — the inverse of the asymmetry the card opened on. That is the staging the card and triage chose (engine half here, spec half on #28059, claimed), the implementation gap is being closed by implementing, not by narrowing a consumer, and the `search` member of those same schemas already refuses `fields: []`. Acceptable; not a finding against this head.

Tried to break it:
- Both slots with conflicting values (`searchFields: ['name']` + `search.fields: []`, and the converse): engine refuses in each case; the declaration refuses each; a POST body is refused at the body schema; a GET cannot spell the object form. No door/engine divergence a caller can observe.
- `searchFields: ['']` (a blank member): engine admits the array as sent (one member), door admits the shape then refuses `''` as an unknown field, declaration admits it (`.min(1)` on length). Engine equals declaration; the residual is the pre-existing unknown-name tolerance (S3), not this rule.
- Hook / flow / `ctx.api` callers that pass an empty override: none in the tree; a third-party one gets the door's answer now, which is the card's intent and the changeset's stated break.
- Error shape under `mapDataError`: pinned by the test; `object` and `param` are set as the door sets them.
- The message's last clause depends on `safeParse([])` failing; it does on `main` and on every head that keeps `.min(1)`; if the declaration were ever widened back the sentence would end in `undefined.` while the refusal stayed — a cosmetic coupling, not a behaviour one.

Findings:

**Must-fix: none.**

**Should-fix S1 — file the runtime seam carrier (noted, not filed).** `packages/runtime/src/stored-metadata-reader-seam.ts:151-154` (`refuseOrNarrowStoredMetadataEvaluate`) calls `narrowStoredMetadataSearch` (protocol.ts 5194), whose explicit-list derivation reads `searchFields: []` as `names.length === 0` and falls into the "names none → NARROW to the allowed set" branch, returning the narrowed default set, which the seam then writes onto the query as `searchFields`. So on a stored-metadata object an in-process host handler's `searchFields: []` with a search term reaches the engine non-empty and is served over the default set, unrefused: the "empty is absent" reading survives one layer above the engine for that object family. At the REST door the same value is refused first by `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable`, so no wire caller sees it. The docblock at protocol.ts 5185-5187 ("an empty override is ABSENT to the engine, which would then scan the whole default set") is false after this PR. Both are outside this claim's surface and the dev reported them; the carrier is unnamed. File it (runtime, `area:api`), naming the seam's residual tolerance and the stale docblock as one card.

**Should-fix S2 — one stale sentence in the spec, for #28059 to carry.** `packages/spec/src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.ts:29-32` says "the in-process engine still reads an empty override as absent." After this PR it does not. The file is `packages/spec` (a breach for this dev); #28059's claimed surface is `data-engine.zod.ts` alone. Ask #28059's seat to amend the surface by this sentence (it is the same accept-set module the card reuses), or file it on #28059's card as a one-line follow-on.

**Should-fix S3 — file the all-unknown override tolerance.** `resolveSearchFields` (search-fields.ts 263-273) still falls back to the whole allowed set when every requested name is outside it; the doors refuse the same value `INVALID_FIELD`. The dev names it the search twin of #27165 and leaves it "noted, not filed". A finding with no card is lost: file it (or name an existing carrier), with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` expected.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4czVnUdQQCVKSW5J2uk`

**VERDICT: PASS**
